reports.title: Pfizer Reports Strong Third-Quarter 2026 Results And Raises 2026 Guidance

guidance.heading: 2026 FINANCIAL GUIDANCE(2)
section: ■Raises full-year 2026 Revenue guidance(2) by $1.5 billion at the midpoint to a range of $62.0 to $64.0 billion from $60.5 to $62.5 billion previously.
■Raises and narrows full-year 2026 Adjusted(3) diluted EPS guidance(2) to a range of $2.95 to $3.05 from $2.80 to $3.00 previously.

–Includes a one-time $650 million Acquired In-Process R&D charge related to the in-licensing and collaboration agreement with Innovent Biologics, Inc. recorded in the third quarter of 2026 with an unfavorable impact of approximately $0.10.
■The company’s guidance takes into consideration our strong year-to-date performance, continued confidence in our business and progress with ongoing cost improvement initiatives.

Revenues | $62.0 to $64.0 billion
Adjusted(3) SI&A Expenses | $12.5 to $13.5 billion
Adjusted(3) R&D Expenses | $10.8 to $11.8 billion
Effective Tax Rate on Adjusted(3) Income | Approximately 15.0%
Adjusted(3) Diluted EPS | $2.95 to $3.05

desk.headline: Revenue flat at $16.6bn and adjusted EPS of $0.87, both beats; 2026 revenue and EPS guidance raised
results: Revenue was flat at $16.6bn; excluding Comirnaty and Paxlovid it grew 7% operationally, and launched and acquired products grew 32%.
Eliquis (+25%), Padcev (+55%), Vyndaqel (+12%), Nurtec (+33%) and Lorbrena (+43%) offset sharp drops in Paxlovid (-63%), Comirnaty (-29%) and Prevnar (-10%).
Adjusted EPS was unchanged at $0.87 despite a $650m Innovent licensing charge (about $0.10 a share); reported EPS fell to $0.56 from $0.62, with $791m of restructuring and deal costs.
R&D spending rose 18% to $3.0bn, driven by cancer and obesity programmes.
$7.3bn paid in dividends over nine months ($1.29 a share); no buybacks, and none assumed in 2026 guidance.

guidance.summary: Pfizer raised its 2026 revenue range by $1.5bn at the midpoint to $62–64bn and raised and narrowed adjusted EPS guidance to $2.95–3.05, even after absorbing the Innovent charge. It plans to give 2027 guidance in mid-December.

points: Management expects 2027 to be a transition year as patents expire on Ibrance and Xtandi in the US and Eliquis abroad, partly offset by new products and cost cuts.
Nearly all of the $7.2bn net savings programme should be delivered by end-2026, with a second phase targeting $2.5bn more over 2027–2029.
Obesity remains a major push: 10 late-stage trials planned in 2026 and a first approval for its monthly GLP-1 shot targeted for 2028.
CEO Albert Bourla said he does not expect US drug-pricing policy changes and sees the pricing agreements holding.
He repeated the aim of high single-digit annual revenue growth from end-2028 to end-2033.
call.source: Call coverage: BigGo Finance, 3 Nov 2026, and The Motley Fool, 4 Nov 2026 (prepared remarks on the company website, not filed)

watch: 2027 guidance in mid-December and how large the patent-expiry hit is.
Obesity trial progress and further pipeline readouts.
Delivery of the second $2.5bn cost-savings phase.
